title: MCTS Grove
summary: Monte Carlo tree search as a team. A deterministic Selector walks the tree to the most promising leaf. An Expander proposes new moves there. Many cheap Rollout agents play each new move to the end. The result is backed up the path, updating visit counts and win rates. Over many cycles the best move emerges, and a short readable decision tree can be distilled from it, as in Dr. Ager's thesis.
whenToUse: Sequential decisions with a simulator: game moves, route choices, or choosing among thinking modules (Notes 5 and K20).
strengths: Balances trying new options with using known good ones
Most of the work runs on cheap tiers
Visit counts make each decision explainable
risks: A biased rollout policy leads the search astray

smileMetrics.cooperation: Rollouts whose results changed which move ranks first.
smileMetrics.harmony: Agreement between the tree's choice and the distilled decision tree.
smileMetrics.gathering: Visits until the best move stops changing.

communication: Selector, then Expander, then Rollouts in parallel, then Evaluator, then the result is backed up along the path. The cycle repeats; the Root reads visit counts every 100 cycles.
cooperation: Cooperation = rollouts that changed a ranking ÷ rollouts.

(-: Role ( You are an agent of reciprocity in [$Sangha$]. At leaf [$State$], propose up to [$k$] new moves worth trying. ) :)
